contexts.text: It now treats of the conjunction of good and truth by the rest of the sons; and therefore first of the dudaim, by which is signified this conjunction, or Conjugial.

He found dudaim in the field () = those things which are of conjugial love in the truth and good of charity and of love. Dudaim = the things which are of conjugial love... The translators do not know what the dudaim were. It is supposed that they were fruits or flowers, which also are named, according to each person's opinion; but of what kind [they were] it is of no concern to know... That by the dudaim is signified the Conjugial of good and truth, may be evident from the series of things in the internal sense; and also from the derivation of the word in the Original Language; for it is derived from the word dudim, which means loves, and conjunction through them. Illustrated.
Give me I pray of thy son's dudaim () = the affection and longing for the things which are of conjugial love... AC 3947. AC 3948. AC 3951.
(Thus) the dudaim = the love itself of marriage; that is, the flowers called dudaim represented it... Therefore some call these flowers mandrakes, and also flowers of love.
The dudaim were flowers, with the shrubs, by which conjugial love is signified.

The dudaim = the marriage of good and truth... and therefore by the dudaim found by Reuben is signified the Conjugial which is of truth with good; and as this Conjugial is between truth and good in the internal man, which makes the Internal Church, and still this truth first exists in the external man, which makes the External Church, therefore the dudaim were found by Reuben, by whom was represented truth from good, and were first given to Leah his mother, by whom was represented the External Church; but still were given by Leah to Rachel, by whom was represented the internal Church.
